Massie Questions GOP Motives On SAVE Act

Massie’s criticism followed a broader warning he posted Sunday on X. "Government can lie to you. Government has lied to you. Government is lying to you. Government will lie to you," he wrote. "Live your life accordingly."
When a user responded by criticizing congressional dysfunction and pointing to public support for voter identification laws, Massie turned his skepticism toward Republicans.
"Don’t waste too much time believing republicans are actually trying to pass the SAVE Act, versus using it as political messaging for partisan advantage ahead of the midterms," he replied.

The Republican-controlled House passed the SAVE America Act 218-213 on Feb. 11, with Texas Rep.

(D) the only Democrat voting yes. The bill requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship, such as a passport or birth certificate, to register for federal elections and establishes national photo-identification requirements for voting.

The bigger obstacle is the Senate. Republicans hold 53 seats but generally need 60 votes to overcome a Democratic filibuster. Senate Majority Leader
(R-S.D.) has said the votes simply are not there. Senators left Washington for their August recess without passing the measure despite Trump demanding they remain in session.
Voter ID Support Meets Partisan Divide

Voter ID itself remains broadly popular. An April Reuters/Ipsos poll found 77% of Americans supported identification requirements. However, Reuters found in July that illegal noncitizen voting is rare, while critics argue documentary citizenship requirements could prevent eligible voters without ready access to birth certificates or passports from registering.
